unverified: Month-to-month (non-annual) billing rate for any plan or contact tier: the public pricing page shows only the annual-billing monthly-equivalent price. The Help Center's billing-information article confirms 'Monthly' is one of three billing cadences available in-account (the others being Annual and 'Commit annually pay monthly'), but no Monthly-cadence rate is published on the marketing site, so it could not be captured.

Price of an extra/additional user seat beyond each plan's included seats (Starter can add 1 extra seat; Plus, Pro and Enterprise can add more) — the Help Center confirms the ability to purchase seats but never states a price; it only appears inside the billing/upgrade flow after signing up.

Enhanced CRM add-ons — Pipelines and Sales Engagement (available on Plus, Professional and Enterprise) — have no published price on activecampaign.com or its Help Center. Third-party review sites cite roughly $68/month and $111/month respectively, but those figures could not be confirmed on an ActiveCampaign-owned page, so they are not included.

SMS add-on and SMS-credit pricing: the Help Center's 'Purchase the SMS add-on' article confirms Plus, Pro and Enterprise accounts can buy SMS credits, but the cost is shown only inside an in-app purchase modal after logging in; no per-credit or per-message rate is published on any page we could read.

Custom Reports add-on price (sold separately on Plus and Professional; included free with Enterprise) and Transactional Email add-on price (available on all four plans, built on Postmark) — both are listed as purchasable in the Help Center's plan-overview article with no price shown anywhere public.

Exact meaning and enforcement of each plan's 'Email sends: Nx contact limit' figure (Starter/Plus 10x, Pro 12x, Enterprise 15x) shown in the pricing page's comparison table — it is never explained whether this is a hard monthly send cap, a fair-use guideline, or a maximum list size. See the growing scenario's note for why this matters.

Whether the other five display currencies the pricing page offers (BRL, CAD, AUD, EUR, GBP) are simple FX conversions of the USD price or independently set regional prices; only the default USD selection was captured.

ActiveCampaign HQ (a separate franchise-specific product) is reported by third parties to carry a one-time fee around $4,500; this is a different product line from the four Email plans in this record and was not verified on an ActiveCampaign-owned page, so it is not included.

For websites you verify it gives Site Explorer (1K backlinks and keywords visible at once), Site Audit (5K crawl credits a month per project) and Web Analytics (up to 1M events per project). Social Media Manager (unlimited while in beta), AI Content Helper (1 document a month) and the SEO Toolbar work without verification. Keywords Explorer and Rank Tracker are not included.

trial.summary: No free trial. Ahrefs' help center says 'We don't provide any free trials' and points to the free Ahrefs Free account instead, and the pricing FAQ says Ahrefs never runs discounts. The cheapest paid entry is Starter at $29/month, which renews monthly and can be canceled before the renewal date.

tools.name: ClickFunnels
tools.category: Funnel builder with courses, store, community and email marketing

freeTier.summary: No free-forever plan. The cheapest paid plan is Launch ($81-$97/month). New signups get a free trial instead of an ongoing free tier (see trial).

trial.summary: Launch, Scale and Optimize show a "Start Free Trial" button; Dominate's button reads "Dominate Now" with no trial offered. Clicking "Start Free Trial" opens a 2-step signup ("Create Your Account: Step 1 of 2") that asks only for name and email on step 1; reaching step 2 (which likely asks for billing details) would require submitting real signup data, so the exact trial length and whether a card is required could not be confirmed from ClickFunnels' current site. Third-party sites and ClickFunnels' own "Classic"-product support articles describe a 14-day trial that auto-charges the card on file when it ends, but that support content is explicitly for the legacy ClickFunnels Classic product, not the current platform priced here, so that figure was not carried into this record.

freeTier.summary: Free Forever has no time limit and allows unlimited members and tasks, but caps file storage at 60MB per Workspace, allows 5 Spaces and 100 Automation actions a month, and gives many paid features only as a fixed number of trial 'uses' per Workspace that never reset: 60 each for Custom Fields, Gantt, Timeline, Workload and Dashboards, and 100 for time tracking. Guests on Free Forever get full edit access that can't be limited. Brain AI is a trial of 25 uses for a Workspace of up to 10 people, and AI add-ons can't be bought on Free Forever. ClickUp's FAQ says it offers a grace period when a limit is reached.

trial.summary: No self-serve free trial of the paid plans: ClickUp's add-ons article says 'If you'd like to add a paid plan trial to your Workspace, contact Support.' Every Workspace gets an automatic AI trial (for example 50 Brain uses for a Workspace of up to 10 people on Unlimited or Business), and Free Forever has no time limit. New customers can get a full refund within 30 days of their first paid plan subscription, including add-ons bought with it.

trial.summary: Every plan (Kickstarter, Basic, Growth, Pro) offers a 14-day free trial with no extensions. That page returned a Cloudflare bot-check ('Are you a robot?' / 'Just a moment...') to every method tried: curl with a browser user agent across multiple paths and subdomains (kit.com, www.kit.com, help.kit.com, status.kit.com, convertkit.com), WebFetch, a US-locale headless Chromium (the pre-existing snapshot), and a headed, non-headless Chromium run under Xvfb with the automation-controlled flag masked and a persistent browser profile, given up to 110 seconds to clear the challenge. Kit's own client-side JavaScript (fetched unauthenticated from cdn.kit.com) shows the marketing pricing table pulls live prices from an account-scoped API (app.kit.com/billing/pricing_display/table) that returned 401 Unauthorized without a logged-in session in every attempt (with and without cookies, CSRF token, and Referer/Origin headers set to kit.com). We did not create a Kit account to query that endpoint, because it is built for an existing customer managing their own subscription, not as a public price list, and creating an account purely to extract data would misuse Kit's signup flow.

The 'small' and 'growing' scenarios above therefore report Creator Pro's confirmed 1,000-subscriber starting price ($79/month) rather than its true, higher price at 10,000 and 50,000 subscribers; each scenario's own note flags this explicitly as an unverified floor, not a real quote.

Whether Kit has additional named plans, add-ons, or usage-based charges (e.g. a paid App Store app, extra seats beyond what's included) beyond the three plans recorded here: not found in Kit's Help Center corpus (400+ articles reviewed) or on the pricing page (blocked); no add-ons or usage charges are listed rather than guessed.

scenarios.label: Solo rep, 1 seat, 1,000 contacts, light email marketing
scenarios.assumptions: Standard cinchstack solo sizing: 1 user, 1,000 contacts, 2,000 marketing emails/month, 200 SMS/month. Lite's cap of 2,500 leads+deals per seat comfortably covers 1,000 contacts, and Lite is Pipedrive's cheapest plan, sized for exactly this kind of single-rep setup. Lite has no built-in email sync or bulk email, so to send the 2,000 marketing emails/month, Pipedrive's own answer is the Campaigns add-on, priced by subscriber count and available on every plan including Lite. At exactly 1,000 subscribers this falls entirely within Campaigns' first pricing band ($0.016/subscriber/month paid monthly), so cost = 1,000 x $0.016 = $16.00/month; this figure is unambiguous because 1,000 is exactly the top of that band under either a graduated or a single-rate reading of Pipedrive's tiers. Pipedrive has no native SMS-sending product, so the 200 SMS/month cannot be priced and are not included (see unverified).

scenarios.label: 3-person sales team, Growth plan, 5,000 contacts, email marketing
scenarios.assumptions: Standard cinchstack small sizing: 3 users, 5,000 contacts, 20,000 marketing emails/month, 1,000 SMS/month. A 3-person team doing real follow-up automation needs Growth: Lite has zero email sync and zero automations of any kind in Pipedrive's own plan-comparison data. Growth's 5,000-leads-and-deals-per-seat cap x 3 seats = 15,000, comfortably covering 5,000 contacts. For the 20,000 marketing emails/month, Campaigns is priced by subscriber count held, not by sends, so the relevant figure is the cost to hold 5,000 marketing subscribers. Pipedrive publishes graduated per-subscriber rates (1-1,000 at $0.016; 1,001-2,000 at $0.008; 2,001-25,000 at $0.006, all paid monthly) and says 'the more contacts you add, the less you pay per subscriber' - consistent with a graduated, banded calculation. Applying each band to 5,000 subscribers: 1,000 x $0.016 + 1,000 x $0.008 + 3,000 x $0.006 = $16.00 + $8.00 + $18.00 = $42.00/month. (If Pipedrive instead charges every subscriber at the single rate of the top band reached, the cost would be 5,000 x $0.006 = $30.00/month instead; nothing captured rules this alternate reading out, hence 'medium' confidence.)

scenarios.label: 8-person sales team, Premium plan, 25,000 contacts, email marketing
scenarios.assumptions: Standard cinchstack growing sizing: 8 users, 25,000 contacts, 100,000 marketing emails/month, 5,000 SMS/month. An 8-person team outgrows Growth's caps (50 automations and just 5 nurture sequences company-wide, 1 email sync per seat); Pipedrive's own upsell path is Premium, which raises those to 150 automations, 25 sequences and 3 email syncs per seat, and adds LeadBooster, lead scoring/enrichment and Smart Docs at no extra cost. Premium's 15,000-leads-and-deals-per-seat cap x 8 seats = 120,000, comfortably covering 25,000 contacts. For the 100,000 marketing emails/month, pricing again follows Campaigns' subscriber count (25,000 marketing subscribers), using the same graduated per-subscriber bands as the small scenario: 1,000 x $0.016 + 1,000 x $0.008 + 23,000 x $0.006 = $16.00 + $8.00 + $138.00 = $162.00/month (paid monthly). As with the small scenario, this assumes Pipedrive's tiers are graduated rather than a single blended rate; a single-rate reading would instead give 25,000 x $0.006 = $150.00/month, so confidence is 'medium'.

Web Visitors add-on: only the entry tier (up to 200 organizations, $49/month paid monthly, $41/month billed annually) and the next two published tiers (201-500 orgs at $99/month; 501-2,000 orgs at $299/month) are public. Smart Docs add-on's two published price bands ($39/month lower band, $59/month higher band) are labeled only by an internal 'units 1-30' / 'units 31-100' range in Pipedrive's own pricing data; no page states what is being counted. This is most likely monthly eSignature requests, since Smart Docs' own free trial is metered in 'five signature requests', but that is inference, not a stated fact.

Pipedrive's embedded pricing data lists paid 'Nova' SKUs (nova_v1 through nova_v4, $10-$25 per seat/month, $96-$240 per seat/year), but every page captured about Nova (pipedrive.com/en/nova and its FAQ) states plainly that 'Nova is included in all plans, at no additional cost.' What the paid Nova SKUs are for (e.g. usage beyond a free monthly allotment) is not explained on any page captured, so no Nova add-on price is recorded here.

Whether Campaigns' published per-subscriber rate bands are graduated (each band applied only to the subscribers within it, as assumed in the small/growing scenarios) or a single blended rate (the whole subscriber count charged at the rate of the top band reached) is not stated on any page captured; Pipedrive's own copy ('the more contacts you add, the less you pay per subscriber') is consistent with either reading.

scenarios.label: Solo seller, $3,000/month in sales
scenarios.assumptions: 1 person, 1 staff account (the owner), $3,000/month in sales. WooCommerce itself is free, so the bill is hosting. The sell grid sets no traffic figure and hosts price by visits, so we borrow the site-layer figure of about 10,000 visits/month. Hosting is Pressable Signature 1, billed monthly: $25/month for 1 WordPress install and up to 30K visits. Pressable is on Woo's recommended-host list, and $25 is the bottom of Woo's own $25–$350/month hosting estimate. A basic store needs no paid extension. WooCommerce takes 0% of sales. Card processing is left out: at WooPayments' US rate of 2.9% + $0.30, 2.9% × $3,000 = $87, plus $0.30 per order.

Woo's hosting guide recommends Pressable or Convesio for stores making $10,000–$500,000 a month and calls Pressable the cheaper of the two. Pressable Signature 2, billed monthly, costs $45/month for up to 50K visits. Staff accounts are WordPress users with the Shop Manager role, at no charge. A basic store needs no paid extension. WooCommerce takes 0% of sales. Card processing is left out: 2.9% × $30,000 = $870, plus $0.30 per order, at WooPayments' US rate.

That is still in Woo's $10,000–$500,000/month hosting tier, so the host is again Pressable. Signature 4 covers only 150K visits: $90 + 100 × $1.20 of overage = $210/month. So Signature 5, at $155/month billed monthly for up to 400K visits, is the cheaper fit. Staff accounts are WordPress users with the Shop Manager role, at no charge. A basic store needs no paid extension. WooCommerce takes 0% of sales. Card processing is left out: 2.9% × $150,000 = $4,350, plus $0.30 per order, at WooPayments' US rate.

scenarios.label: Solo operator, 1 seat, on Standard
scenarios.assumptions: 1 user, 1,000 contacts, 2,000 marketing emails and 200 SMS a month. Free is ruled out because it has no Mass Email (bulk send) feature at all; Standard adds it with a cap of 250 mass emails/day per organization (about 7,500/month over 30 days), which comfortably covers 2,000/month. 1,000 contacts is far under Standard's 100,000-record storage cap. Zoho CRM has no native SMS/texting feature on its pricing or feature-comparison pages, so the 200 SMS/month cannot be priced and are not included (see unverified).

scenarios.label: 3-person team, 3 seats, on Enterprise (forced by mass-email volume)
scenarios.assumptions: 3 users, 5,000 contacts, 20,000 marketing emails and 1,000 SMS a month. Org-wide Mass Email caps, extended to a month at 30 days, are Standard 250/day (about 7,500/month) and Professional 500/day (about 15,000/month) - both short of 20,000/month. Enterprise's 1,000/day (about 30,000/month) is the first tier that covers it. 3 seats and 5,000 contacts are both far under Enterprise's other limits regardless. Zoho CRM has no native SMS feature, so the 1,000 SMS/month cannot be priced and are not included (see unverified).

scenarios.label: 8-person team, 8 seats, on Ultimate (mass-email volume exceeds every edition's cap)
scenarios.assumptions: 8 users, 25,000 contacts, 100,000 marketing emails and 5,000 SMS a month. Ultimate is the highest self-serve edition, and its org-wide Mass Email cap (2,000/day, about 60,000/month over 30 days) is still short of the 100,000/month assumption for this layer - no Zoho CRM edition's published limit reaches 100,000/month. Ultimate is used here as the best available fit; reaching 100,000/month natively would need a separate product or a support-approved limit increase not published on these pages (Zoho's own FAQ points large deployments toward migration/consultation services). 8 seats and 25,000 contacts are both far under Ultimate's other limits. Zoho CRM has no native SMS feature, so the 5,000 SMS/month cannot be priced and are not included (see unverified).
